Fibroblasts from the musculocontractural EDS type 2 patient showed significantly decreased DS disaccharide content along with reduced DSE activity compared to healthy subject fibroblasts.
Dse-deficient mice show reduced DSE activity and DS content, smaller body size, kinked tail at birth, and thicker dermal/hypodermal collagen fibrils.
Dse-/- mice additionally exhibited fetal abdominal wall defects, exencephaly, spina bifida, and impaired migration of aortic smooth muscle cells.
Dse-deficient mice showed reduced migration of skin-derived dendritic cells to draining lymph nodes, diminishing initiation of cellular and humoral immune responses.

Knockdown of Dse (but not Dsel) in Xenopus laevis decreased epimerase activity and neural crest cell migration, reducing neural crest-derived craniofacial skeleton, melanocytes, and dorsal fin structures.

DSE knockdown (shRNA) in human esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cells reduced migration, invasion, HGF interaction, pERK1/2 signaling, and focal adhesion/actin dynamics, implicating DSE/DS in tumor progression.
Various homozygous or heterozygous DSEL mutations were reported to cause bipolar disorder.
A single nucleotide polymorphism 75 kbp upstream of DSEL was associated with recurrent early-onset major depressive disorder.
DSEL mutations were reported in probands with congenital diaphragmatic hernia, and Dsel was expressed in murine diaphragm muscle at E13.5.

Dsel-deficient mice showed tissue-specific reductions in epimerase activity (brain 89%, kidney 55%, spleen 44%, liver 38%, lung 34%, skin 24%) but no gross morphological, histological, or anatomical defects.
Double knockout (Dse/Dsel) mice showed complete loss of dermatan sulfate, perinatal lethality, exencephaly, umbilical hernia, and kinked tail, indicating DS is essential for embryonic development.

CHST14 (D4ST-1) mutations were identified in 11 probands from four families with adducted thumb-clubfoot syndrome, a connective tissue disorder with congenital heart/kidney/intestinal defects, skin fragility, and joint contractures; five of eleven died in early infancy or childhood.
Fibroblasts from a patient with CHST14 p.Arg213Pro showed reduced DS with a reciprocal increase in CS compared to control subjects.

CHST14 (D4ST-1) mutations were identified in six probands with EDS characterized by progressive multisystem fragility, spinal deformities, recurrent dislocations, joint/skin laxity, multiple congenital joint contractures, and characteristic craniofacial features.

Recombinant CHST14/D4ST-1 mutants (p.Pro281Leu, p.Cys289Ser, p.Tyr293Cys) expressed in COS-7 cells and patient skin fibroblasts showed markedly lower D4ST enzymatic activity than wild-type/healthy controls.
In skin fibroblasts from CHST14-mutant patients, a chondroitin sulfate chain, rather than dermatan sulfate, was produced on the decorin core protein.

Malfait et al. independently reported EDS kyphoscoliotic type VIB in three probands from two families caused by homozygous CHST14 mutations, leading to the unification of D4ST1-related syndromes as 'musculocontractural EDS,' later adopted as EDS musculocontractural type 1 in the 2017 International Classification.

Neurospheres from Chst14-/- mice showed larger diameters and fewer total numbers than wild-type, reflecting dysfunction in neural stem cell self-renewal and proliferation; the 473HD epitope was decreased to 58% of wild-type levels.

Chst14-/- mice showed a higher proliferation rate and longer cell processes of cultured Schwann cells from nerves and dorsal roots compared with wild-type; one-third of knockout mice died between E16.5-E18.5 or shortly after birth, with reduced kidney, liver, heart, tibia, and body weights (but not brain).

Placentas from Chst14-/- mice showed decreased DS, abnormal capillary basement membrane structure, ischemic/necrotic-like vascular changes, and reduced placental weight compared to wild-type, suggesting D4ST-1/DS is required for placental vascular development.

Chst14-/- mice showed abnormal, linear/rod-shaped decorin GAG chains protruding from collagen fibrils (instead of the normal round, wrapped DS conformation) and reduced skin tensile strength compared with wild-type.

Chst14-/- mice exhibited elongated teeth, thoracic kyphosis, increased skin fragility, kinked tail, reduced muscle DS disaccharide, and myopathy-related phenotypes (interstitium spreading, fiber size variation) potentially linked to decreased exercise capacity and lower grip strength.

Skin biopsies from musculocontractural EDS probands showed dispersed, disorganized collagen fibrils in the papillary to reticular dermis (vs. tight regular assembly in controls), with linear CS-substituted decorin GAG chains stretching between fibrils instead of the curved DS chains seen in controls.

Urinary DS was absent in patients with pathogenic CHST14/D4ST1 variants, detected via anion-exchange HPLC with chondroitinase B digestion, suggesting utility as a non-invasive screening test for the disorder.
Knockdown of D4ST-1 (CHST14) in human lung fibroblasts caused a marked reduction of IdoUA-containing structures in the dermatan sulfate chain.
DSE, but not DSEL, forms a heterocomplex with D4ST-1 that is essential for synthesizing longer IdoUA-containing dermatan sulfate chains.
Neurospheres from Chst14-deficient mice showed larger diameters and fewer total numbers than wild-type, reflecting dysfunction in self-renewal and proliferation of neural stem cells.
In neurospheres from Chst14-deficient mice, the 473HD epitope, which marks specific CS/DS sulfation motifs, was decreased to 58% of wild-type levels.
Chst14-deficient mice showed cultured Schwann cells from nerves and dorsal roots with a higher proliferation rate and longer cell processes compared with wild-type.

One third of Chst14-deficient mice died between embryonic day 16.5-18.5 and/or shortly after birth, and surviving knockouts had reduced kidney, liver, heart, tibia, and whole-body weights compared with wild-type littermates, while brain weight was unaffected.

Placenta derived from Chst14-deficient mice showed significantly decreased DS, abnormal capillary basement membrane structure, ischemic/necrotic-like vascular changes, and reduced placental weight compared with wild-type.

In wild-type mice, DS side chains of decorin adopted a round conformation wrapping collagen fibrils, whereas in Chst14-deficient mice, rod-shaped linear CS side chains protruded outside the fibrils, and skin tensile strength was reduced.

Chst14-deficient mice exhibited elephant teeth, thoracic kyphosis, increased skin fragility, kinked tail, reduced muscle DS disaccharide, and myopathy-related changes (spread muscle interstitium, variable fiber size) associated with decreased exercise capacity and lower grip strength.

Adducted thumb-clubfoot syndrome in 11 probands from four families was caused by homozygous CHST14 mutations p.Val49*, p.Arg213Pro, and p.Tyr293Cys, and a compound heterozygous mutation p.Arg135Gly/p.Leu137Gln.
Fibroblasts from a patient with CHST14 p.Arg213Pro mutation showed a reduced amount of dermatan sulfate and an increase in chondroitin sulfate compared with control subjects.

Kosho et al. (2005) reported two probands with generalized joint laxity, scoliosis, skin fragility, hyperextensibility, easy bruising, atrophic scars, hypotonia, recurrent hematomas, pectus excavatum, and mild delay of gross motor development, proposing EDS kyphoscoliosis type VIB.

Miyake et al. identified CHST14 mutations (compound heterozygous p.Lys69*/p.Pro281Leu, p.Pro281Leu/p.Cys289Ser, p.Pro281Leu/p.Tyr293Cys, or homozygous p.Pro281Leu) in six probands with the EDS phenotype originally described by Kosho et al. (2010).

Recombinant CHST14/D4ST-1 mutants p.Pro281Leu, p.Cys289Ser, and p.Tyr293Cys expressed in COS-7 cells showed markedly lower D4ST enzymatic activity than wild-type, and skin fibroblasts from patients with p.Pro281Leu or p.Pro281Leu/p.Tyr293Cys also showed considerably weaker D4ST activity than healthy subjects.

In skin fibroblasts from patients with CHST14 mutations, a chondroitin sulfate chain was produced on the decorin core protein instead of dermatan, consistent with loss of 4-O-sulfation permitting reverse epimerization of IdoUA to GlcUA by DSE.

Skin biopsies from musculocontractural EDS probands showed dispersed, irregularly assembled collagen fibrils in the papillary to reticular dermis compared with tightly regular fibrils in controls, and decorin GAG side chains were altered from curved DS to linear CS conformation, stretching between adjacent fibrils rather than remaining in close contact.

Mizumoto et al. (2017) demonstrated absence of urinary DS in patients with pathogenic CHST14/D4ST1 variants using anion-exchange HPLC with chondroitinase B, indicating urinary disaccharide compositional analysis as a non-invasive screening method for the disorder.

Malfait et al. (2010) independently reported that EDS kyphoscoliotic type VIB in three probands from two families was caused by homozygous CHST14 mutations p.Val49* and p.Glu334Glyfs*107, and proposed unifying D4ST1-related syndromes (the novel EDS and adducted thumb-clubfoot syndrome) as 'musculocontractural EDS,' later adopted as EDS musculocontractural type 1 in the 2017 International Classification of EDS.

Foot deformities are a common orthopaedic complaint in patients with connective tissue and related disorders including Down syndrome, Marfan syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Larsen syndrome, and osteogenesis imperfecta.
Increased ligament laxity, hypotonia, and joint hypermobility are cited as common underlying causes of foot deformities in these connective tissue disorders, including Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Treatment options for syndromic foot deformities described include foot orthoses, physical therapy, bracing, and various surgical procedures.

The authors note there is limited evidence supporting surgical intervention to correct foot deformities associated with these connective tissue disorders including Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and further research is needed.

Cultured fibroblasts from an mcEDS-CHST14 patient (patient 6) secreted chondroitin sulfate (CS) but no dermatan sulfate (DS) into the medium, replicating the glycosaminoglycan abnormality previously reported for patient 3.

Collagen gels seeded with mcEDS-CHST14 patient-derived fibroblasts showed significantly larger diameters and delayed contraction at 1 and 3 hours compared to gels with healthy control fibroblasts, though diameters equalized by 24 hours.

Transmission electron microscopy showed that the proportion of collagen fibrils assembled into fibers was markedly lower in gels cultured with patient-derived fibroblasts (38.9% and 50.0%) than with control fibroblasts (68.2%).

Scanning electron microscopy showed no significant difference in mean collagen fibril diameter between control and patient-mimicking gels, but fibril diameter distribution was more heterogeneous in patient-mimicking gels than in controls.
Patient-mimicking collagen gels reached failure at significantly lower maximum stress than control gels, indicating weaker mechanical strength resulting from impaired fibrillar organization.

GAG chains of decorin isolated from mcEDS-CHST14 patient fibroblasts were misoriented and did not tightly attach to collagen fibrils, unlike the evenly spaced, vertically oriented GAG chains of control decorin.

Collagen fibers and fibrils formed in vitro with patient-derived decorin had significantly smaller diameters than those formed with normal decorin, demonstrating impaired decorin function in mcEDS-CHST14.
Fibroblasts from Chst14-/- mice produced collagen fibrils with smaller diameter than fibroblasts from Chst14+/+ and Chst14+/- mice, with GAG chains not tightly aligned on fibrils.

Decorin from Chst14-/- mice skin was resistant to chondroitinase B (DS-specific) but digested by chondroitinase ABC, indicating DS chains on decorin were replaced by CS chains, consistent with prior findings in mcEDS-CHST14 patients.
Collagen gels incubated with decorin isolated from two independent Chst14-/- mice had significantly smaller fibril diameters than gels incubated with decorin from Chst14+/+ and Chst14+/- mice.
Removal of three retained Weck polymer clips from the gallbladder fossa in a patient with EDS and MCAS resulted in complete resolution of her hypersensitivity reaction symptoms at one-week follow-up.
A prior study of 195 medical records found that MCAS prevalence was 31% among patients with both POTS and EDS compared to 2% in patients without POTS and EDS, a statistically significant difference.
Mast cell activation syndrome can arise from neoplastic gain-of-function mutations most commonly affecting KIT, a receptor tyrosine kinase highly expressed on mast cells.
A referenced clinical trial found that imatinib, a signal transduction inhibitor, decreased mast cell tryptase levels and mast cell numbers.
EDS comprises six main subtypes caused by different mutations in genes responsible for collagen synthesis.
The patient's treating immunologist attributed worsening joint pain and facial swelling following orthopedic procedures to medical implants triggering mast cell activation.
Pregnant patients with EDS were more likely to be older, white, and have comorbidities including smoking, mitral valve prolapse, and chronic hypertension compared to those without EDS.
After adjusting for maternal age and race, patients with EDS were more likely than those without EDS to require Cesarean-section delivery.
Adjusted analysis showed patients with EDS were more likely to develop postpartum hemorrhage than those without EDS.
Adjusted analysis showed patients with EDS were more likely to experience intrauterine growth restriction than those without EDS.
Adjusted analysis showed patients with EDS were more likely to deliver preterm than those without EDS.
Despite higher rates of other maternal complications, aortic aneurysmal rupture was not found to be increased among patients with EDS.

In a 16-year-old female with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and heavy menstrual bleeding, placement of the LNG-IUD under ultrasound guidance in the operating room led to significant improvement in bleeding and high patient satisfaction at 6-month follow-up, with no complications noted at placement or follow-up.

Heavy menstrual bleeding is reported to be common among adolescents with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and LNG-IUD use in vascular EDS patients has historically been avoided due to perceived risk of uterine rupture.
Dermatan sulfate was not detectable in the urine or skin fibroblasts of patients with mcEDS-CHST14.
DS was absent or significantly decreased in skin fibroblasts and urine of patients with mcEDS-DSE.
Dse gene-deleted (Dse-/-) mice showed a reduction, but not complete loss, of IdoUA blocks characteristic of dermatan sulfate in whole body and skin, suggesting residual activity of DSEL.
Dse-/- mice on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvJ background had a slightly lower-than-Mendelian birth rate, while Dse-/- mice on a pure C57BL/6 background showed perinatal lethality.
Dse-/- pups and adult mice were smaller and lighter than wildtype littermates.
Dse-/- mice showed a 41% reduction in skin tensile strength with altered collagen fibril ultrastructure, despite unchanged collagen and decorin content.
Dse-/- mice showed decreased dermal dendritic cell migration and immune response to ovalbumin, with fewer CD4+/CD8+ T cells and antigen-specific B cells/immunoglobulins.
Dsel-/- mice had decreased epimerase activity and IdoUA content in brain and kidney but showed no anatomical, histological, or morphological abnormalities and had a normal lifespan.

Dse-/-;Dsel-/- double-knockout (DKO) mice showed complete loss of IdoUA residues in CS/DS at 2 days old and died in the perinatal period, with some embryos showing umbilical hernia, exencephaly, and kinked tail.
Binding of the chemokine CXCL13 to embryonic fibroblasts was impaired in Dse-/-;Dsel-/- double-knockout mice despite normal development of secondary lymphoid organs.
Chst14-/- mice showed embryonic lethality between E16.5 and E18.5, with only 1.9% of Chst14-/- pups surviving birth or postnatally versus 14.8% present at E18.5.

Placentas of Chst14-/- embryos showed decreased Chst14 expression and DS content, reduced weight, ischemic/necrotic-like changes, decreased villus volume, and abnormal capillary basement membrane structure with rupture.
Chst14-/- mice required 75% less force to rupture skin probes than Chst14+/+ mice and had reduced body/organ weights.

Detailed histological analysis showed skin tensile strength decreased to one-fourth in Chst14-/- mice, with disorganized, variably-oriented collagen fibrils and deformed GAG chains protruding from fibrils, compared with well-organized fibers in wildtype mice.

CRISPR/Cas9-generated Chst14-/- mice showed a sixfold increase in chondroitin sulfate in skeletal muscle and significantly decreased decorin expression, which was mislocalized to both perimysium and endomysium.

Chst14 mutant mice showed a myopathy phenotype with predominance of small muscle fibers and type I fibers, thoracic kyphosis at 1 year, and significantly and consistently weaker grip strength and decreased motor function (voluntary activity, running speed) from 2 to 12 months of age.

Chst14-/- Schwann cells formed longer processes with increased proliferation, neurite lengths of cerebellar neurons and motoneurons were increased, and functional recovery after femoral nerve injury was significantly accelerated in Chst14-/- mice.

After severe compression injury of the spinal cord, regeneration was reduced in Chst14-/- mice compared with Chst14+/+ littermates, although baseline spinal cord size and glial cell numbers were unaffected.

Chst14-/- mice showed deficits in spatial learning and memory with significantly decreased hippocampal synaptic plasticity proteins (GAP43, synaptophysin, NSF, NMDAR1, NMDAR2A, NMDAR2B, GluR1, PSD95) and decreased phosphorylation of Akt, mTOR, and S6.
DS disaccharides were markedly decreased in cultured fibroblasts from a patient with mcEDS-DSE compared with a healthy control, with DSEL insufficient to compensate for DSE loss.
Skin fragility and hyperextensibility were more prevalent in mcEDS-CHST14 patients than in mcEDS-DSE patients (skin fragility 90% vs 29%; hyperextensibility 100% vs 57%).
Large subcutaneous hematomas, a serious mcEDS symptom, were reported in 81% of mcEDS-CHST14 patients and 67% of mcEDS-DSE patients, but this phenotype has not been reproduced in mouse models.

In Chst14-/- mouse skeletal muscle, myostatin (a negative regulator of protein synthesis) and TGF-β were upregulated while decorin expression was decreased, accompanying muscle fibrosis and growth suppression.
Large CAH cohort studies have shown that approximately 15% of CAH patients carry a contiguous gene deletion disrupting both CYP21A2 and TNXB, producing concomitant hEDS (CAH-X).

A TNXA pseudogene variant carrying two SNPs in tandem (rs4959086 and rs77471377) converts the TNXA locus to be TNXB exon 40-like, causing a falsely elevated TNXB exon 40 copy number by ddPCR in true CAH-X-negative subjects.
The TNXB-like TNXA variant allele had an overall allele frequency of 10.3% (48 of 467 TNXA alleles) in the CAH cohort.
The TNXB-like TNXA variant allele was most frequently found in cis with a normal CYP21A2 allele, accounting for 45.8% (22/48) of variant alleles.
The TNXB-like TNXA variant allele was the second most common found in cis with the CYP21A2 In2G pathogenic variant, accounting for 25.0% (12/48) of variant alleles.
At least 13.3% of chromosomes with a normal CYP21A2 allele and 11.8% of chromosomes with an In2G CYP21A2 allele carried one or more copies of the TNXB-like TNXA variant.
In a control group of 29 subjects with normal TNXB exon 40 copy number, no rs77471377(C>G) variant was detected, while four carried the rs4959086(C>G) SNP alone.

When a subject carries a CAH-X CH-2 chimera together with at least one TNXB-like TNXA variant, the true TNXB exon 40 copy number loss can be masked, creating a risk of false-negative CAH-X CH-2 calls by ddPCR-based copy number testing.

A CAH carrier with a CAH-X CH-1/normal genotype showed atypical TNXB exon 35 and 40 copy numbers (1 and 2, respectively, instead of 1 and 1) due to a TNXB-like TNXA variant on her normal chromosome, illustrating in-trans masking interference.

The authors' previously developed ddPCR-based CAH-X screening assay had 99.3% overall accuracy (276/278) but showed excess TNXB exon 40 copy number in 45 of 234 true CAH-X negatives, versus only one such discrepancy at exon 35.

CAH-X patients have about 25% prevalence of cardiac abnormalities, including structural valve abnormalities, left ventricular diverticulum, and patent foramen ovale, beyond typical joint/skin manifestations.

Given CAH carrier prevalence of 1 in 60 and that roughly one-third of CAH alleles are 30-kb deletions of which one-third are CAH-X chimeras, CAH-X among CAH carriers alone is estimated to affect 1 in 670 in the general population, consistent with the possibility that hEDS prevalence (1 in 5000) is underestimated.

Of current high-throughput CAH genetic test platforms (qPCR, MMCP, MLPA), only MLPA tests TNXB exon 35 copy number (useful for CAH-X CH-1), while TNXB exon 40 is entirely outside the scope of these standard platforms.

The authors conclude that standard NGS-based methodologies are not yet suitable for genetic testing of RCCX module genes within the homologous window, applying both to CYP21A2 and to TNXB exons 32-44, due to pseudogene interference and underestimated variant allele frequencies.

The gnomAD population database reports allele frequencies of 0.1795 for rs4959086 and 0.02 for rs77471377, which the authors argue underestimate the true frequency of the tandem TNXA variant haplotype (10.3-13.3% by chromosome-based counting in this cohort) because TNXA copy number varies from 0-4 per chromosome, invalidating standard diploid allele frequency calculations.
Hutch Diverticulum, a congenital bladder wall defect at the vesicoureteral junction, may be associated with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Williams-Elfin syndrome, and Menkes syndrome.
The pooled prevalence of fracture among patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome was 44%.
The pooled prevalence of fracture among patients with Marfan's syndrome was 17%.
The pooled prevalence of fracture among patients with Loeys-Dietz syndrome was 69%.
The pooled prevalence of osteoporosis among patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome was 17%.
EDS was significantly associated with fracture, with a pooled odds ratio of 4.90 compared to healthy individuals.
EDS was not significantly associated with osteoporosis compared to controls, suggesting fracture risk is independent of bone mineral density status.
One study reported a 5% prevalence of osteoporosis in Marfan's syndrome patients.
Marfan's syndrome was associated with increased incidence of fracture, with an incidence rate ratio of 1.35.
In patients with Marfan's syndrome, one study reported a significantly increased subhazard ratio for osteoporosis of 3.97.

Pre-treatment with the selective β2-adrenergic receptor blocker butoxamine (10 or 30 mg/kg) before the second acid injection prevented the development of mechanical hypersensitivity in the acid-induced generalized pain (AcGP) mouse model of fibromyalgia.

Carazolol, a peripheral β2-adrenergic blocker with lower blood-brain barrier permeability than butoxamine, also dose-dependently prevented the development of acid-induced mechanical hypersensitivity, indicating the effect occurs peripherally rather than in the CNS.

When butoxamine or carazolol was administered after hypersensitivity was already established (P5 to P11), the drugs did not reverse the PWT decrease, indicating β2-adrenergic receptors are not involved in maintenance of established hypersensitivity.

Prazosin, an α1-adrenergic receptor blocker, did not prevent development of acid-induced mechanical hypersensitivity, indicating α1-adrenergic receptors are not required for pain development in this model.
Butylscopolamine, an anticholinergic drug, did not affect development of mechanical hypersensitivity in the AcGP model, indicating cholinergic signaling is not a major driver of pain development.

Adoptive transfer of splenocytes from AcGP donor mice pre-treated with butoxamine (β2 blocker) failed to induce mechanical hypersensitivity in naïve recipient mice, showing that β2-adrenergic receptor activation in donor mice is necessary for splenocytes to acquire pain-inducing capacity.

Pre-treatment of donor AcGP mice with prazosin (α1-blocker) had no effect on the ability of transferred splenocytes to induce PWT decrease in recipient mice, indicating α1-adrenergic receptors are not required for splenocyte-mediated pain reproduction.

Multiple clinical studies cited by the authors describe elevated sympathetic activity with reduced parasympathetic tone in patients with fibromyalgia, supporting a rationale for autonomic/sympathetic involvement in FM pathophysiology.
Individuals with fibromyalgia have lower brain GABA levels in sensory processing regions compared to healthy controls.
Anticonvulsant medications that modulate GABA, such as pregabalin and gabapentin, show some efficacy as fibromyalgia treatment.
Females with major depression are 1.34 times more likely to respond and 1.37 times more likely to achieve remission than males with tDCS treatment.
Around half of women in two studies reported fibromyalgia symptoms after childbirth, with a higher rate following cesarean versus vaginal delivery.
Pregnant women with pre-existing fibromyalgia experienced aggravation of symptoms throughout pregnancy, worst in the third trimester.
Women with fibromyalgia experience more pain during the luteal phase and perimenstrual period compared with healthy controls.

In transgender individuals, 55% of female-to-male people with chronic pain reported pain reduction after testosterone treatment, while 23% of male-to-female individuals reported new chronic pain onset after estrogen and anti-androgen therapy.
ERβ agonists alleviated chemotherapy-induced pain in an animal model, whereas the nonselective agonist 17β-estradiol and ERα-selective agonist PPT had no effect.

In premenopausal women with fibromyalgia, progesterone and testosterone (but not estradiol or cortisol) were inversely correlated with pain severity, with pain highest during menses when gonadal hormones were lowest.
Progesterone and its metabolite allopregnanolone reduce neuropathic pain via allosteric stimulation of GABAA receptors in animal models.
Cortisol production increases from the end of the first trimester, reaching serum levels of about 50 µg/dL by the end of gestation.
Hypocortisolism has been observed in about one-quarter of patients with stress-related disorders, including fibromyalgia.
Prolactin increases the synthesis and release of GABA in hypothalamic tissue.
Some reports show low serotonin serum levels in fibromyalgia patients, proposed as a potential biomarker.
In pregnant women with fibromyalgia, serotonin decreases as pregnancy progresses, associated with increased anxiety and depression and possibly contributing to late-pregnancy pain recrudescence.
Pregnant female rodents show reduced brain GABA levels and downregulation of GABAA receptor δ and γ2 subunits.
The first randomized, sham-controlled proof-of-principle study of tDCS in 2006 provided initial evidence of therapeutic effect in fibromyalgia.

Across six studies of tDCS in major depressive disorder or auditory hallucinations during pregnancy, no serious pregnancy or birth complications were observed over more than 120 and 160 tDCS sessions, respectively, with minimal anticipated side effects and general patient satisfaction.
Both migraine and irritable bowel syndrome are cited as common fibromyalgia comorbidities within the Central Sensitivity Syndrome category.
Fibromyalgia rates become female-dominant starting at puberty, unlike the more even sex distribution in pre-pubertal children.
Under the 'pregnenolone steal' hypothesis, stress-driven cortisol synthesis may divert pregnenolone away from progesterone/allopregnanolone synthesis, causing their depletion.
At the highest physiological concentrations, allopregnanolone can invert its action on the α4β2δ GABAA receptor subunit combination from activation to inhibition.
5-HT2A receptors decrease pain when estrogen levels are high, while 5-HT2A antagonist blockage increases the estrogen-induced pain release.
In a web-based survey of over 600 patients with post-COVID syndrome, about 30% met 2011 ACR criteria for fibromyalgia at a mean of 6 months after COVID-19 recovery, termed post-COVID FM.
Obesity and male gender were identified as risk factors for developing post-COVID FM-like syndrome in the surveyed cohort.
Severe COVID-19 requiring hospital admission and oxygen therapy was suggested to be more predictive of developing post-COVID FM-like syndrome.

A separate cohort found that 56.7% (17/30) of patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 were positive for FM-like symptoms 6 months after infection, suggesting disease severity is not required for development of post-COVID FM-like syndrome.

Three previously-healthy women developed generalized musculoskeletal pain, allodynia, fatigue, anxiety, depression, paraesthesia, and non-restorative sleep after COVID-19 recovery, and all met 2010 ACR criteria for fibromyalgia despite normal autoimmune and radiologic work-up.
In the same three-patient case series, standard FM treatment with duloxetine, gabapentin, and physical exercise improved well-being and mood, supporting the post-COVID FM-like syndrome diagnosis.
In a case report, acetaminophen, NSAIDs, and opioids failed to relieve a post-COVID patient's FM-like pain, mirroring the typical unresponsiveness of FM pain to these agents.
In the same case, gabapentinoid treatment attenuated painful hypersensitivity and improved sleep quality, consistent with gabapentinoids' efficacy in FM.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, FM patients experienced greater mental stress and anxiety, and exacerbated pain, fatigue, and sleep quality compared with COVID-19 patients without FM.
Fear and anxiety levels during the COVID-19 pandemic were higher in FM patients than in controls without FM.
In a survey of 32 FM patients, 67% reported worsened general health/well-being during COVID-19 lockdown.
All 129 FM patients in an Israeli study who used non-pharmacological treatments interrupted these activities after COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, and over half lost contact with their physician.
FM patients appear more susceptible to mood disorders than patients with other rheumatic diseases in the COVID-19 pandemic setting.
Cytokines TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8 are found at higher serum levels in both COVID-19 and fibromyalgia patients, suggesting a shared inflammatory mechanism.

Pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines gradually decreased from symptom onset to 12 months post-COVID as fatigue, weakness, and sleep problems attenuated, supporting an inflammatory basis for these symptoms.
Both COVID-19 and fibromyalgia show impaired mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production, culminating in mitochondrial membrane permeabilization and mitophagy.
Increased levels of malondialdehyde, a marker of oxidative stress, have been observed in both COVID-19 and fibromyalgia patients.
Significantly lower vitamin D levels have been shown in COVID-19 patients (correlated with disease progression) and in some FM patients.
Neuropilin-1, expressed in nociceptors, has been reported as a host cell entry receptor for SARS-CoV-2, providing a potential mechanistic link between viral entry and nociceptor sensitization.
Dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons are a potential target for SARS-CoV-2 invasion, and viral infection of nociceptors may cause persistent neurological effects seen in COVID-19.
Dysregulated immune processes in fibromyalgia produce autoreactive IgG antibodies that bind antigens expressed in the dorsal root ganglia, potentially increasing noxious peripheral input.
Autoantibodies against cytokines and chemokines in COVID-19 patients appear to perturb immune function and impair virological control, potentially contributing to peripheral sensitization.
Pregabalin, alone or with antidepressants, relieved pain symptoms in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
In two ICU COVID-19 pneumonia patients, adding pregabalin significantly reduced cough, chest pain, and myalgia, and improved tolerance of non-invasive ventilation and prone positioning.
Evidence indicates pregabalin use is not associated with increased in-hospital mortality among COVID-19 patients.
One study reported contradictory findings that pregabalin use was associated with an increased incidence of COVID-19 in patients.
Duloxetine, an FDA-approved FM drug, was associated with decreased incidence of COVID-19 in patients using it.
A telerehabilitation aerobic exercise program relieved painful symptoms and psychological distress in women with FM during the COVID-19 pandemic.

IL-6 released by macrophages is a key driver of the cytokine storm and its elevation is associated with COVID-19 severity, with tocilizumab and sarilumab (anti-IL-6 receptor monoclonal antibodies) approved for severe COVID-19.

JAK inhibitors (baricitinib, tofacitinib, ruxolitinib) targeting the IL-6-activated JAK/STAT pathway have been trialed in COVID-19 with proven effectiveness in critically ill patients but inconsistent conclusions on mortality reduction.

Large-scale randomized trials showed corticosteroids contribute to recovery of severe or critically ill COVID-19 patients, but long-term use requires careful evaluation due to potential adverse effects on multiple organ systems.

Several additional anti-inflammatory drug classes (colchicine, inhaled corticosteroids, IL-1 inhibitor anakinra, BTK inhibitors, NSAIDs) have been tested for COVID-19 but remain investigational and are not FDA-approved or panel-recommended for this indication.
Duloxetine, an FDA-approved FM therapy, was associated with decreased incidence of COVID-19 in patients in one study.

One study reported contradictory effects of pregabalin, including an increased incidence of COVID-19 in patients who used it, contrasting with other studies showing pregabalin was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality.

Amitriptyline, imipramine, paroxetine, and sertraline have potential antiviral activities of interest for COVID-19, and amitriptyline showed potential benefit for patients with post-COVID headaches, and relieved pain when combined with pregabalin in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
Tizanidine, a muscle relaxant used for myofascial pain and FM, could potentially be repositioned for treating post-COVID-19 symptoms.
A telerehabilitation program based on aerobic exercise relieved painful symptoms and psychological distress in women with FM during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Significantly lower levels of vitamin D have been observed in patients with COVID-19, correlating with disease progression, and low vitamin D is also reported in some patients with FM.
Vitamin D therapy could improve quality of life in FM patients and reduce COVID-19 progression while enhancing survival rate.
Neuropilin 1, expressed in nociceptors, was recently reported as a host entry receptor for SARS-CoV-2, suggesting a mechanism for viral invasion of pain-sensing neurons.

Dysregulated immune processes produce autoreactive IgG antibodies that bind antigens expressed in the dorsal root ganglion of FM patients, potentially increasing noxious peripheral input, similar to autoantibodies against cytokines/chemokines seen in COVID-19 that impair virological control.
Increased levels of malondialdehyde, an oxidative stress marker, have been observed in patients with both COVID-19 and FM.

Antioxidant therapeutic strategies successfully reverted severe symptoms in COVID-19 patients and also reverted several symptoms of FM, supporting a shared role for oxidative stress in both conditions.

Pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines gradually decreased from symptom onset to 12 months post-COVID as fatigue, weakness, and sleep problems were attenuated, supporting a role for inflammation in symptom development.
Fear and anxiety levels during the COVID-19 pandemic were higher in patients with FM compared to control patients without FM.
67% of 32 patients with FM reported that their general health status (well-being) worsened during the COVID-19 lockdown.
In an Israeli study, all 129 FM patients using non-pharmacological treatments interrupted their activities after COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, and over half lost contact with their physician.
Patients with FM appear to be more susceptible to mood disorders than patients with other rheumatic diseases in the COVID-19 pandemic setting.
The most commonly self-reported cause of exacerbating FM symptoms during pandemic restrictions was inability to exercise.
Among proposed diagnostic criteria for neurological post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection, 60% (25 of 42 reported symptoms) matched criteria for FM diagnosis.

Obesity and male gender were identified as risk factors for developing post-COVID FM-like syndrome, and severe COVID-19 (hospital admission, oxygen therapy) was more suggestive of developing this syndrome.
Fibromyalgia patients had significantly higher intramuscular pressure in the trapezius muscle compared to healthy controls.
A biopsy study found peripheral fibroblast TGF-β gene expression is significantly higher in fibromyalgia patients compared to controls.
Fibromyalgia patients had significantly lower amounts of intramuscular collagen, which may lower the threshold for muscle micro-injury.
Fibromyalgia patients show decreased peripheral blood flow, suggesting functional cardiovascular disturbances.
Muscle biopsies from fibromyalgia patients show increased DNA fragmentation and ultrastructural changes, suggested to be secondary to chronic muscle contraction.
Fibroblasts from fibromyalgia patients show differential protein expression of genes involved in ECM turnover and oxidative metabolism, potentially explaining an inflammatory status.

Microdialysis studies of the trapezius muscle show that myofascial pain syndrome patients have increased concentrations of nociceptive and inflammatory substances (substance P, interleukins, TNF-alpha) in myofascial tissue.
Fibromyalgia patients have higher levels of lactate and pyruvate in myofascial tissue, consistent with local ischemia.

A randomized controlled trial found that both dry needling and extracorporeal shockwave therapy significantly lowered fascia shear modulus (stiffness) at 1 month post-treatment compared to pre-treatment, correlating with reduced pain and increased pressure pain thresholds.
In the same trial, shear modulus increased again by 3 months post-treatment compared to 1-month values, suggesting a partial relapse of fascial stiffness reduction.
A study comparing trigger points and traditional acupuncture points for pain found approximately 70 percent correspondence between the two sets of points.
A study suggested tissue stiffness of approximately 20 kPa is the threshold for robust myofibroblast α-SMA synthesis, relevant to when needling might reverse myofibroblast activity.
Systematic reviews and meta-analyses report that acupuncture alleviates pain and stiffness in fibromyalgia and myofascial pain syndrome.
Multiple studies using shear wave elastography show that needling therapy lowers the shear modulus and stiffness of myofascial tissue.
Patients with Ehlers-Danlos/hypermobility syndrome show widespread ECM disarray and an increase in myofibroblasts.
There is a reported close association between hypermobility/Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and fibromyalgia/psychosomatic disease, suggested to share common pathophysiology.
Allodynia and hyperalgesia in fibromyalgia can be improved or abolished by removal of peripheral impulse input, indicating a peripheral contribution to central sensitization.

The fascial armoring model proposes that fibromyalgia pathophysiology involves mechano-signaling of myo/fibroblasts via integrin/focal adhesion, Rho-associated kinase (ROCK), α-SMA, and TGF-β pathways, generating fascial tension.

The author's central hypothesis is that acupuncture functions mechanically as a global percutaneous needle fasciotomy respecting biotensegrity principles ('tensegrity-based needling'), which could relieve myofibroblast-generated fascial tension and treat fibromyalgia-like syndromes.
Duodenal mast cell activation correlates with symptom pattern and burden in functional dyspepsia and can be associated with gastric sensorimotor dysfunction.
Duodenal eosinophil activation correlates with symptom pattern and burden in functional dyspepsia and can be associated with gastric sensorimotor dysfunction.
Duodenal bile salt exposure correlates with symptom pattern and burden in functional dyspepsia and can be associated with gastric sensorimotor dysfunction.
Proton pump inhibitors, the current first-line treatment, reduce duodenal low-grade inflammation and symptoms of functional dyspepsia.
The authors propose that future FD treatment research should target inhibition of duodenal mast cell activation, eosinophilia, and loss of mucosal integrity.
Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced sepsis significantly increased hippocampal levels of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β and IL-10 at 24 hours compared with sham mice.
CLP-induced sepsis significantly reduced 7-day survival rate in mice compared with sham surgery mice.
CLP mice showed marked cognitive deficits, including reduced exploratory movement and time in center in the open field test, and reduced movement/time in the novel zone in the Y maze.

Mast cell number and activation (TB-positive and tryptase-positive cells) were increased in the hippocampal CA1 region of septic (CLP) mice compared with sham mice, and hippocampal tryptase levels were elevated.
Intracerebroventricular cromolyn (mast cell stabilizer) given before and after CLP surgery significantly inhibited hippocampal mast cell activation compared with saline-treated CLP mice.
Cromolyn pretreatment mitigated CLP-induced elevation of intracerebral inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-10) and improved 7-day survival in septic mice.
Cromolyn treatment increased movement distance and time in center in the open field test and improved Y maze performance in septic mice, indicating alleviation of CLP-induced cognitive impairment.

Brain water content, and fluorescein sodium (FS) and Evans blue (EB) extravasation into hippocampus and brain were significantly increased in CLP mice, indicating BBB permeability breakdown, and this was reversed by cromolyn.
Hippocampal MMP2 and MMP9 protein expression increased significantly in CLP mice while tight junction proteins ZO-1, occludin and claudin-5 were sharply reduced; cromolyn reversed both changes.
LPS stimulation of P815 mast cells significantly increased β-hexosaminidase release (degranulation marker), an effect alleviated by cromolyn treatment.
LPS stimulation increased histamine, tryptase, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-10 release from P815 mast cells, an effect partially reversed by cromolyn.

LPS stimulation increased apoptosis (Tunel+) and decreased proliferation (Ki67+) of bEnd.3 brain microvascular endothelial cells, and this dysfunction was worsened when co-cultured with P815 mast cells; cromolyn partially rescued BMVEC viability.
LPS upregulated MMP2/MMP9 and downregulated ZO-1, occludin and claudin-5 in bEnd.3 cells, with changes augmented by mast cell (P815) co-culture and reversed by cromolyn.

LPS treatment upregulated H1R, TLR2 and TLR4 expression and increased phosphorylation of P38, P42/44 and JNK MAPK signaling proteins in bEnd.3 cells, with effects augmented by mast cell co-culture and ameliorated by cromolyn.

Overexpression of H1R in bEnd.3 cells markedly increased LPS-induced TLR2, TLR4 expression, MAPK (P38, P42/44, JNK) phosphorylation, and inflammatory cytokine (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-10) release compared with control cells.
siRNA knockdown of H1R in bEnd.3 cells decreased LPS-induced TLR2/4-MAPK signaling and inflammatory cytokine production, opposite to the effect of H1R overexpression.
Cromolyn treatment alone (without CLP surgery) did not alter mast cell activation in the brain, indicating its effect is specific to sepsis-induced activation.
Inotodiol, administered orally in a lipid-based formulation, showed mast cell-stabilizing activity in mouse anaphylaxis models that was equally potent to dexamethasone.
Inotodiol was four to over ten times less effective than dexamethasone at suppressing other immune cell subsets besides mast cells, with the magnitude varying by subset.
Inotodiol preferentially and more profoundly affects membrane-proximal signaling required for mast cell activation compared to signaling in other immune cell subsets.
Inotodiol effectively prevented asthma exacerbation in the studied model.
The no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) of inotodiol was over 15 times higher than that of dexamethasone, giving inotodiol a therapeutic index at least eight times better than dexamethasone.

In systemic mastocytosis, neoplastic mast cell aggregates in the gastrointestinal tract and other sites show atypical morphology and aberrant CD25 immunostaining in addition to tryptase and CD117 positivity.
Increased mast cell numbers have been reported in gastrointestinal mucosal biopsy samples from patients with irritable bowel syndrome.
Increased mast cell numbers have also been reported in gastrointestinal mucosal biopsies from patients with hereditary alpha-tryptasemia.

Patients with mast cell activation syndrome are thought to experience symptoms from aberrant release of histamine and other mediators from normal-appearing mast cells that are present in normal numbers, rather than from increased mast cell counts.

Neoplastic mast cell disorders such as systemic mastocytosis are characterized by bone marrow and gastrointestinal/skin mast cell aggregates whose mediator release causes diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal pain.
Serum intestinal permeability indices and bacterial DNA levels were markedly higher in antihistamine-resistant chronic spontaneous urticaria patients than in those without resistance.
Bacterial DNA levels positively correlated with the degree of inflammation in chronic spontaneous urticaria patients.
IL-6 and TNF-alpha levels were upregulated in LAD2 mast cells stimulated with bacterial DNA in a time- and dose-dependent manner.
Bacterial DNA-induced cytokine production in LAD2 cells depended on unmethylated CpG motifs and Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) protein.
Syk knockdown or inhibition of Syk Tyr525/526 phosphorylation blocked bacterial DNA-initiated cytokine production in LAD2 cells.
Nedd4L interacted with Tyr525/526-phosphorylated Syk, and Sgk1-induced inhibition of Nedd4L Ser448 phosphorylation was required for bacterial DNA's proinflammatory effect.
Sgk1 suppression exerted an inhibitory effect on bacterial DNA-induced inflammation by preserving Nedd4L-mediated ubiquitination of Tyr525/526-phosphorylated Syk.
The Small Fiber Neuropathy-Symptom Inventory Questionnaire (SFN-SIQ) failed to distinguish between patients confirmed to have small fiber neuropathy and those without it.

A 43-year-old woman developed painful, spreading small-fiber neuropathy 3-4 weeks after her second mRNA-1273 (Moderna) SARS-CoV-2 vaccine dose, confirmed by skin biopsy showing reduced intraepidermal nerve fiber density.

Passive surveillance data (VAERS) show a very small number of reported peripheral neuropathy or paresthesia events relative to the large number of Americans fully vaccinated with Pfizer, Moderna, or Janssen SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, suggesting SFN is a rare complication.
A novel heterozygous SCN9A mutation, p.L951I (c.2851C>A), was identified in a 9-year-old child with severe primary erythromelalgia.
Immunofluorescence of the affected leg skin showed decreased intraepidermal nerve fiber density, consistent with small fiber neuropathy in this primary erythromelalgia case.
Substance P expression was not increased in lesional (affected) skin tissue compared to expectations for neurogenic inflammation.
CGRP expression was not increased in the lesional skin tissue, suggesting it does not play a major pathophysiological role in this case of primary erythromelalgia.
Corneal nerve fiber density measured by in vivo corneal confocal microscopy was significantly decreased in CIDP patients compared to healthy controls.
Corneal nerve fiber length was significantly decreased in CIDP patients compared to healthy controls.
Corneal Langerhans cell density was increased in CIDP patients compared to controls, suggesting an immune/inflammatory component.
Corneal nerve fiber tortuosity was increased in CIDP patients compared to controls.

IVCCM parameters were significantly lower in CIDP patients with neuropathic pain compared to CIDP patients without neuropathic pain, indicating a link between corneal small fiber loss and pain symptoms.
Among 920 ICI-treated cancer patients, 20 developed a peripheral nervous system immune-related adverse event (PNS-irAE), an overall incidence of 2.17%.
The frequency of PNS-irAEs increased across ICI class from PD-1 (1.8%) to PD-L1 (2.9%) to CTLA-4 (4.3%) to combination PD-1+CTLA-4 therapy (7.1%).
Four patients developed an acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (GBS-like) with CSF albuminocytologic dissociation and electrodiagnostic evidence of demyelination.
Three patients developed ICI-related cranial neuropathies, including unilateral facial palsy and bilateral vestibulocochlear neuropathy, which were largely steroid-refractory.

Three patients developed ICI-induced small-fiber neuropathy, presenting with subacute painful paresthesia, anhidrosis, and reduced pain/heat sensation, with electrodiagnostic evidence of absent skin sympathetic response and otherwise normal nerve conductions.
One patient developed acute painless right brachial pan-plexopathy with CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein following ICI therapy.
In patients with ir-neuropathies, immunosuppressive treatment and/or ICI withdrawal was associated with significant improvement in modified Rankin Scale scores.
Among four patients with ir-neuropathy who were rechallenged with the same ICI after complete resolution of neurological symptoms, none experienced neurological relapse.
All patients diagnosed with ICI-induced myasthenia gravis tested positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor (AchR) antibodies, with a mean titer of 1.84 nmol/L.
Serum creatine kinase (CK) levels were markedly elevated in patients with ICI-induced myositis (with or without concurrent MG), ranging from 380 to 21,700 IU/L.
Anti-titin antibodies were detected in three of four patients (75%) with concurrent MG/myositis/myocarditis, consistent with prior reports linking this autoantibody to overlap syndromes.
Unlike neuropathy patients, those with MG/myositis did not show a statistically significant improvement in mRS with immunosuppression and ICI withdrawal.
Patients with MG/myositis had significantly higher mortality than those with neuropathies (44% vs 0%).
Time from ICI initiation to symptom onset was significantly shorter in patients with MG/myositis than in those with neuropathies.
Concurrent non-neurologic irAEs were significantly more common in patients with MG/myositis than in those with neuropathies.

The authors hypothesize that pre-existing anti-AchR antibody positivity, even when asymptomatic, may predispose patients to develop or exacerbate ICI-induced myasthenia gravis, based on one patient with known well-controlled MG who suffered fatal myasthenic crisis after two nivolumab infusions.

Four of six patients with concurrent MG/myositis also had myocarditis, consistent with the previously described IM3OS (myositis-myasthenia-myocarditis) overlap syndrome, which the literature associates with high mortality (up to 60%).

The observed frequency of ICI-induced neuromuscular/peripheral nervous system adverse events in this cohort was higher than rates reported in prior clinical trial systematic reviews (<1%) and large retrospective cohorts (1.22-1.5% for all n-irAEs, 0.6% for severe neuromuscular events).
Higher serum VEGF levels were positively associated with maximum skin temperature of the thenar eminence of the non-dominant hand in women with fibromyalgia.
Serum VEGF levels were positively associated with the minimum skin temperature of the thenar eminence of the non-dominant hand in women with fibromyalgia.
Serum VEGF levels were positively associated with the mean skin temperature of the thenar eminence of the non-dominant hand in women with fibromyalgia.
Serum VEGF levels were positively associated with the maximum skin temperature of the hypothenar eminence of the non-dominant hand in women with fibromyalgia.
Despite several significant associations, the overall relationship between serum VEGF and hand skin vasodilation in fibromyalgia patients was described as mild and inconclusive.
In the supine position, diabetic patients had significantly higher craniocaudal diameter, anteroposterior diameter, and cross-sectional area of the gastric antrum than non-diabetic controls.
In the right lateral decubitus position, diabetic patients showed significantly higher craniocaudal diameter, anteroposterior diameter, and cross-sectional area than controls.
Calculated fasting gastric volume was significantly higher in diabetic patients than in non-diabetic controls.
Fasting interval duration was comparable between diabetic and non-diabetic groups.
Autonomic dysfunction in diabetics is proposed as the underlying mechanism for gastropathy and delayed gastric emptying, increasing aspiration vulnerability.

A cited external study (Rajeswari) reported that diabetics had significantly higher antral cross-sectional area and estimated gastric residual volume than non-diabetics in both right lateral and semi-recumbent positions.

A cited external study (Haramgatti et al.) found significantly higher nasogastric tube aspirate volume in diabetics compared to non-diabetics despite both groups having minimal residual gastric volume overall.

A cited external study (Sabry et al.) found diabetics had greater median antral CSA, higher estimated gastric residual volume, and larger aspirated NG tube gastric volume than controls, with strong correlation between ultrasound and NG aspirate measures.

A cited external study (Sharma et al.) found that 10-hour fasting did not ensure an empty stomach and that diabetes increased the likelihood of hazardous residual gastric contents on bedside ultrasound.
A cited external study reported that despite following current preoperative fasting guidelines, about 50% of type 2 diabetes patients still had a full stomach.
Serum vitamin B12 levels were significantly lower in patients with type 2 diabetes compared with healthy controls.
The frequency of vitamin B12 deficiency (defined as <125 pmol/L) was 35% among T2D patients versus 0% in healthy controls.
Vitamin B12 levels were significantly lower in T2D patients with gastroparesis than in those without gastroparesis.
Vitamin B12 deficiency was much more frequent in T2D patients with gastroparesis (54.5%) than in those without gastroparesis (11.1%).
Vitamin B12 level was negatively correlated with GCSI (symptom severity) score in T2D patients with gastroparesis.
Vitamin B12 level was positively correlated with gastric emptying percentage in T2D patients with gastroparesis.
Vitamin B12 level was positively correlated with antral motility index in T2D patients with gastroparesis.
Vitamin B12 deficiency was an independent positive predictor of diabetic gastroparesis on multivariable logistic regression.
A serum vitamin B12 cutoff of 189.5 pmol/L predicted gastroparesis in T2D patients with 69.1% sensitivity and 64.4% specificity.
Longer duration of type 2 diabetes was an independent predictor of gastroparesis.
Higher BMI was an independent predictor of diabetic gastroparesis.
Female sex was an independent predictor of diabetic gastroparesis.
Higher HbA1c was a strong independent predictor of diabetic gastroparesis.
Higher fasting plasma glucose was an independent predictor of diabetic gastroparesis.
Higher total cholesterol was an independent predictor of diabetic gastroparesis.
Higher triglycerides were an independent predictor of diabetic gastroparesis.
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was significantly more frequent in patients with gastroparesis and an independent predictor of gastroparesis.
Diabetic retinopathy (proliferative) and nephropathy were significantly more frequent in gastroparesis patients and were independent predictors of gastroparesis.
Ultrasonographic gastric emptying percentage and antral motility index were significantly lower in T2D patients with gastroparesis compared with those without.
The GCSI symptom score did not significantly differ between T2D patients with and without gastroparesis, despite ultrasonographic differences.
IBS model rats showed increased abdominal wall retraction reflex (AWR) scores compared with controls, indicating visceral hypersensitivity.
IBS model rats showed a decreased visceral pain threshold (PT) compared with controls.

IBS model rats displayed sympathovagal imbalance with increased LF and LF/HF ratio and decreased HF power on ECG-derived heart rate variability, indicating sympathetic dominance and autonomic imbalance.
IBS model rats had a decreased frequency of slow waves on intestinal electromyogram compared with controls, reflecting impaired intestinal electrical activity.
IBS model rats showed a marked decrease in HF power of heart rate variability compared with control rats, indicating reduced parasympathetic tone.
IBS model rats had a reduced frequency of slow waves in intestinal electromyography compared with control rats, indicating impaired colonic motility.
IBS model rats exhibited a lower visceral pain threshold than control rats, consistent with visceral hypersensitivity.
Colonic TH protein expression and immunoactivity were markedly decreased in IBS model rats compared with controls, indicating reduced sympathetic innervation markers.

Electroacupuncture at ST36 alone and at ST36 combined with ST25 both significantly reduced AWR, LF, and LF/HF ratio compared with the model group, indicating decreased sympathetic-dominant autonomic imbalance and visceral hypersensitivity.
Electroacupuncture at ST36 alone and at ST36+ST25 both significantly reduced colonic ChAT protein expression and immunoactivity compared with the model group.
Electroacupuncture at ST36 alone significantly reduced the elevated colonic ChAT protein expression and immunoactivity seen in IBS model rats.
Electroacupuncture at ST36 alone increased colonic TH protein expression and immunoactivity that had been reduced in IBS model rats, indicating restored sympathetic marker levels.
Electroacupuncture at ST36 reduced the elevated serum cAMP and cGMP contents and cAMP/cGMP ratio observed in IBS model rats.
Electroacupuncture at ST36 reduced visceral hypersensitivity (AWR) and sympathovagal imbalance (LF, LF/HF) that were elevated in the IBS model rats.
EA-ST36+ST25 combined treatment increased slow wave frequency of intestinal EMG and visceral pain threshold, similar to EA-ST36 alone, restoring levels reduced in model rats.
Combining ST36 and ST25 electroacupuncture did not produce an apparent synergistic effect compared with ST36 electroacupuncture alone in improving IBS-related autonomic and colonic function measures.
Women reported a higher prevalence than men of problems with writing, reading, and counting at all three post-infection time periods (<4, 4-12, and >12 weeks).
Women reported greater difficulty with thoughts communication than men across all three post-infection time periods.
A sex difference in reporting problems answering questions in an understandable/unambiguous manner was significant only in the 4-12 week post-infection window, with women more affected.
Women reported more difficulty recalling new information than men, significant below 12 weeks post-infection (<4 and 4-12 weeks) but not after 12 weeks.
No sex differences were found in reported problems with multitasking, remembering past information, determining the current date, or field orientation.
Fatigue was the most common Long COVID symptom, reported by 48.3% of symptomatic participants.
Other common Long COVID symptoms included shortness of breath (22.9%), confusion/brain fog (22.7%), headache (21.6%), and altered taste or smell (20.6%).
A greater number of acute COVID-19 symptoms during initial infection was associated with higher odds of prevalent Long COVID symptoms across all three multivariable models.

Participants infected during later SARS-CoV-2 variant waves (Delta, Omicron) were less likely to report Long COVID symptoms than those infected earlier, despite shorter follow-up time, even after adjusting for vaccination status.
Hispanic ethnicity was associated with higher odds of Long COVID symptoms after adjustment for vaccination, ethnicity, and social determinants of health.
Lower subjective socioeconomic status (MacArthur Scale) was associated with higher odds of Long COVID symptoms.
Vaccination status, whether before or after infection, was not statistically significantly associated with Long COVID symptoms.
Pre-existing depressive symptoms (measured before SARS-CoV-2 infection using PHQ-8) were associated with higher odds of subsequently reporting Long COVID symptoms.
Pre-COVID financial insecurity was associated with higher odds of Long COVID symptoms.
Among participants with pre-COVID baseline data, those who developed Long COVID had a greater decrease in physical activity frequency after COVID-19 compared with those without Long COVID.
About half of participants with Long COVID symptoms reported ongoing symptoms at time of survey, and among those infected more than a year prior, 56.1% still had symptoms.
In sensitivity analysis restricted to persistent symptoms, female sex was associated with higher odds of persistent Long COVID symptoms, unlike the main model.
Participants who later reported Long COVID symptoms had a higher baseline symptom burden even in the 30-60 days before SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to those who did not develop Long COVID.

Longitudinal daily/weekly surveys showed a substantially higher proportion of symptom reporting among those with Long COVID compared to those without Long COVID and those never infected with SARS-CoV-2 at 180-365 days post-infection.
ME/CFS patients showed significantly higher rates of a positive attention deficit indicator on CPT3 compared to healthy controls, with about 70% of patients positive versus 30% of controls.
Inattentiveness scores were significantly higher/more atypical in ME/CFS patients than in healthy controls on CPT3.

Vigilance, the ability to maintain performance at slower stimulus rates, was significantly different between ME/CFS patients and controls, though with a smaller effect size than inattentiveness or attention deficit.
Impulsivity and sustained attention indicators from CPT3 were both significantly different between ME/CFS patients and healthy controls in chi-square tests of independence.
Gender was found to be a significant variable in the chi-square analysis distinguishing ME/CFS patients from controls, despite gender imbalance not being controlled for in study design.
ME/CFS patients showed significantly slower Hit Reaction Time (HRT), a measure of information processing speed, compared to healthy controls.

HRT SD, reflecting consistency of response speed, was significantly higher in ME/CFS patients, indicating greater inconsistency in response speed and possible reduced engagement/processing efficiency.

Response speed Variability was significantly elevated in ME/CFS patients, and a threshold value of 60 was identified above which patients were rarely found in the control group, suggesting risk of cognitive impairment.
Detectability, the ability to discriminate targets from non-targets, was significantly poorer in ME/CFS patients than in controls (Student's t-test), indicating inattention.
HRT Block Change (slope of reaction time across the six test blocks) and HRT ISI Change (slope across interstimulus intervals) were not significantly different between ME/CFS patients and controls.

A random forest model using CPT3 features classified ME/CFS patients versus controls with 77.19% accuracy on a held-out test set, with HRT, Detectability, and Variability as the most important discriminating features.

Spearman correlation network analysis among ME/CFS patients (P group) showed five CPT3 numerical variables forming a fully interconnected network (all pairwise correlations >0.5), while three variables were unrelated to the rest.
A relevant number of ME/CFS patients had CPT3 scores compatible with a moderate-to-high likelihood of having an attention-deficit disorder resembling ADHD, more so than controls.
Nearly all Long COVID respondents (79 of 80) reported experiencing post-exertional malaise, the hallmark symptom of ME/CFS.
Chi-square analyses showed significant differences between Long COVID and ME/CFS patients in the types of exertional triggers that provoke PEM.
Both Long COVID and ME/CFS patients reported that low and medium levels of physical and cognitive exertion could trigger PEM, indicating similarity between groups on this domain.
Both groups reported similar symptom clusters during PEM, including fatigue, pain, immune-related reactions, neurologic symptoms, orthostatic intolerance, and gastrointestinal symptoms.
Significant differences were found between Long COVID and ME/CFS patients in ways they recover from and prevent PEM.
Both Long COVID and ME/CFS patients reported using rest to recover from PEM and pacing to prevent PEM.
Just over half of AAV patients (27/52, 51.9%) fulfilled diagnostic criteria for ME/CFS despite having clinically inactive vasculitis (BVAS=0).
Among AAV patients with ME/CFS, 37% (10/27) also met diagnostic criteria for fibromyalgia.
Vasculitis subtype (GPA, MPA, EGPA) was not associated with presence of ME/CFS-defined fatigue.
A trend was observed toward higher rates of ME/CFS in MPO-ANCA positive patients compared to PR3-ANCA positive patients among AAV-CFS patients.
Vasculitis damage index (VDI) scores were significantly higher in AAV patients with ME/CFS compared to those without.
Eye involvement was significantly more common in AAV patients with ME/CFS compared to those without.

Non-fatigued AAV patients (AAV-NCFS) closely resembled healthy controls and differed significantly from fibromyalgia patients on cognitive failure, anxiety, depression, sleep disturbance, pain (WPI), fatigue severity (SSS, MFI), and quality of life (SF-36).

AAV patients meeting ME/CFS criteria (AAV-CFS) showed similar rates of cognitive failure, anxiety, and sleep disturbance, and similar fatigue severity (MFI), compared to fibromyalgia patients, suggesting phenotypic overlap.
In PR3-ANCA patients, fatigue was associated with higher rates of cognitive failure, arthralgia, female sex, and higher CRP levels.
In MPO-ANCA patients, fatigue was associated with pain as measured by the widespread pain index (WPI), with trends for fibromyalgia and anxiety.

PR3-AAV-CFS patients had significantly lower rates of anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbance compared to fibromyalgia patients, whereas MPO-AAV-CFS patients had similar rates of these symptoms to fibromyalgia patients.
Both PR3- and MPO-AAV-CFS patients had lower widespread pain (WPI) scores than fibromyalgia patients.
MPO-AAV-CFS patients reported more lower back, abdominal, and lower leg pain compared to PR3-AAV-CFS patients, who mostly reported neck, shoulder and upper back pain.
MPO-AAV-CFS patients were significantly older than PR3-AAV-CFS patients.
Depression and quality of life (SF-36) were significantly correlated with fatigue severity (MFI) in both PR3-ANCA and MPO-ANCA patients.
Sleep disturbance was significantly correlated with fatigue severity in MPO-ANCA patients specifically.
Disease-related factors such as VDI, organ involvement, and medication history were not correlated with fatigue severity in either serotype.
Anxiety was significantly more prevalent in MPO-ANCA patients compared to PR3-ANCA patients overall.
Kidney involvement, arthralgia, and positive biopsy pathology were significantly more prevalent in PR3-ANCA patients compared to MPO-ANCA patients.
Arthralgia was unexpectedly more prevalent in non-fatigued PR3-ANCA patients compared to fatigued PR3-ANCA patients.
A personal narrative describes a young woman physical therapist who developed ME/CFS following COVID-19 infection, highlighting gaps in rehabilitation professionals' education about the condition.

The narrative notes that ME/CFS patients are often referred to rehabilitation professionals who frequently lack appropriate education and experience treating this patient population, and evidence-based treatments for ME/CFS remain scarce.
Approximately 43% of adult ME/CFS patients surveyed via a patient blog forum reported that their illness onset occurred prior to age 18.

Qualitative content analysis of patient blog commentary identified recurring themes among adults recalling childhood ME/CFS onset, including poor mental health, family history of illness, a healthy childhood preceding sick adulthood, feeling misunderstood, delayed diagnostic clarity, poor school functioning, isolation/poor social supports, and coping mechanisms.
Among PASC patients with persistent symptoms beyond six months, 43% (45/105) fulfilled IOM criteria for ME/CFS.
Female PASC patients reported significantly more symptoms than male patients (median 13 vs 10).
Fatigue, insomnia, and dysgeusia were significantly more common in female than male PASC patients.
Symptom frequency correlated strongly with symptom severity across the PASC cohort.
Fatigue, post-exertional malaise, brain fog, unrefreshing sleep, and daytime sleepiness were the most prevalent symptoms in the PASC cohort.
Principal component analysis showed that fatigue, post-exertional malaise, daytime sleepiness, brain fog, and unrefreshing sleep clustered together as co-occurring symptoms resembling ME/CFS.
Obesity (BMI >30 kg/m2) was significantly more common in the ME/CFS-PASC subgroup compared with the rest of the PASC cohort.
Worse functional status (FSS level 4 or 5) was significantly more prevalent in the ME/CFS-PASC subgroup than the broader PASC cohort.
The majority (82%) of PASC clinic patients had some degree of functional limitation, and 33.9% had significantly compromised wellbeing.
Persistent PASC symptoms at initial clinic visit ranged in duration from 34 to 792 days, with a median duration of 285.5 days.
Obesity was the most common comorbidity in the PASC cohort, present in 35.1% of patients, among comorbidities predisposing to severe disease.
The large majority (87%) of PASC patients had not required hospitalization or oxygen for acute COVID-19, indicating that PASC/ME-CFS phenotype occurs frequently even after mild acute illness.

At the first assessment (initial two weeks post-infection), an exploratory factor analysis of self-reported symptoms produced three factors: Cognitive Dysfunction, Autonomic Dysfunction, and Gastrointestinal Dysfunction.
At the second assessment (mean 21.7 weeks later), the factor analysis yielded Cognitive Dysfunction, Autonomic Dysfunction, and Post-Exertional Malaise as the three symptom factors.

Autonomic Dysfunction and Gastrointestinal Dysfunction factor scores measured at time 1 significantly predicted overall pandemic-related functional impact (Coronavirus Impact Scale summary score) at time 2.
The same time-1 Autonomic Dysfunction and Gastrointestinal Dysfunction factor scores predicted subsequent occurrence of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) at time 2.
Graded exercise therapy (GET) and cognitive behavior therapy (CBT) did not improve employment outcomes among people with ME/CFS.
Peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak) decreased significantly from Test-1 to Test-2, indicating failure to reproduce baseline aerobic capacity 24 hours after the first exercise test.
Oxygen consumption at the ventilatory threshold (VO2@VT) decreased by 16.4% between Test-1 and Test-2, substantially exceeding normal test-retest variability.
Peak O2 pulse, a surrogate for stroke volume/cardiac output, decreased by 4.9% between Test-1 and Test-2, indicating compromised oxygen delivery following PEM induction.
All measures at maximal exercise intensity (HRpeak, peak minute ventilation, peak CO2 production) decreased in Test-2 compared to Test-1.
At ventilatory threshold intensity, all measured variables (HR@VT, Ve@VT, O2pulse@VT) similarly decreased during Test-2 compared to Test-1.
The six-minute walk test distance decreased from Test-1 to Test-2, indicating reduced functional exercise capacity following post-exertional malaise induction.
The time required to reach VO2peak and VO2@VT was significantly lower in Test-2 than Test-1, suggesting earlier attainment of the anaerobic threshold post-exertion.
Respiratory exchange ratio at peak effort (RERpeak) was ≥1.1 in both tests and did not differ between Test-1 and Test-2, confirming maximal effort was achieved in both CPETs.

The authors propose that PHMG-p, a main toxic component of humidifier disinfectants, causes mitochondrial dysfunction across cell types, which could underlie the CFS symptoms observed in HD-exposed individuals, though this mechanism was not directly tested in the study.

In a single moderate-quality RCT of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome, pain neuroscience education produced short-term improvements versus self-management education on some psychosocial subscales (pain catastrophizing 'rumination', pain coping 'distraction' and 'worrying'), but showed no significant difference on other catastrophizing/coping domains or kinesiophobia scores.

Across two RCTs with low-to-moderate risk of bias, PNE combined with usual multidisciplinary fibromyalgia treatment was more effective than usual treatment alone across outcomes including pain impact (FIQ), pain severity/interference (BPI), functional status (HAQ), anxiety/depression (HADS), and pain catastrophizing (PCS).

In two moderate-to-high-quality RCTs, PNE given as a stand-alone intervention was not more effective than education-and-relaxation or self-management instruction for fibromyalgia patients in the short or medium term.

In the single RCT on chronic spinal pain, PNE produced greater short-term (2-week) improvement than neck/back school education on pain catastrophizing and pain disability, regardless of participants' baseline central sensitization inventory level, though no long-term benefit was assessed.

In a chronic low back pain RCT, PNE combined with therapeutic exercise was more effective than exercise alone for kinesiophobia and pain catastrophizing at both follow-ups and for pain intensity and disability at 3 months.
PNE combined with aquatic exercise showed similar results to aquatic exercise alone in chronic low back pain patients.
PNE added to physiotherapy showed no significant difference compared with physiotherapy alone in chronic low back pain patients.
A culture-adapted ('sensitized') PNE approach for Turkish patients showed no significant difference from standard PNE, though both produced significant within-group improvement over time.
At an 8-week follow-up, PNE alone was significantly more effective than PNE combined with aerobic exercise for pain (VAS) and disability (RMDQ) scores in chronic low back pain patients.

In a different chronic low back pain RCT, PNE combined with aerobic exercise was more effective than a comparator for pain (NPRS) and psychosocial factors (PSEQ) at 8 weeks, but the effect lost statistical significance by 3 months.

PNE combined with dry needling was more effective than dry needling alone for reducing kinesiophobia (TSK-17), reaching the minimal clinically important difference (MCID>8), but not for disability or pain measures.

A three-arm RCT found PNE plus manual therapy and home exercise produced significantly greater improvement in kinesiophobia at both follow-ups versus manual therapy and home exercise alone, and greater improvement in kinesiophobia, pain, and disability versus home exercise alone.

Study eligibility for central-sensitization-dominant chronic MSK pain was operationalized using CSI scores >40 and/or positive quantitative sensory testing, or via diagnostic labels/psychosocial criteria (e.g., fibromyalgia, CFS, maladaptive pain beliefs) when explicit CSI/QST data were unavailable.

Overall, across 15 RCTs, pain neuroscience education improved pain, disability, and psychosocial factors in patients with persistent musculoskeletal pain and central sensitization, with only two studies finding no significant superiority over controls on any outcome.

An internet-based recruitment strategy using a single Facebook group for older adults with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome yielded 32 participants within two weeks, supporting feasibility of this recruitment method.

Nearly all participants reported satisfaction with the survey's length, clarity and navigation, and 10 participants offered free-text suggestions for improvement, supporting the usability of the survey instruments.
Baseline survey data suggest that older women with hEDS/HSD experience a high symptom burden and poor health-related quality of life.
The patient carried two novel compound heterozygous PLOD1 variants causing lysyl hydroxylase 1 (LH1) deficiency, confirming a diagnosis of kEDS-PLOD1.

The patient developed multiple arterial complications in her 30s, including a thrombosed occlusive aneurysm and dissection of tibial arteries and a dissecting aneurysm of the tibial-peroneal trunk, demonstrating vascular fragility in kEDS-PLOD1.
Progressive kyphoscoliosis led to restrictive lung disease with a forced vital capacity of 40%, requiring noninvasive ventilation.
Muscle biopsy revealed asymmetric axonal sensorimotor neuropathy and demyelinating neuropathy in the legs, likely underlying bilateral perforating plantar ulcers.
The patient developed progressive myopia, open-angle glaucoma, bilateral scleromalacia, corneal thinning, and peripheral retinal fragility.
Osteodensitometry showed femoral osteopenia in the patient.
Echocardiography revealed a myxoid mitral valve without prolapse and a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 43%.

Severe lumbar pain from disc herniation was pharmaco-resistant, and invasive options (infiltrations, discectomy) were excluded due to vascular fragility risk, with palliative rehabilitation strategies preferred instead.
Authors recommend early beta-blocker therapy and blood pressure monitoring as secondary prevention against arterial complications in kEDS-PLOD1.
A systematic vascular evaluation revealed splenic infarctions without identified trauma and a small ectasia of the splenic artery.
The patient developed urinary and bowel incontinence along with a renal angiomyolipoma.
The patient required anticoagulant treatment for an idiopathic pulmonary embolism, with negative thrombophilia screening.
The patient had generalized joint hypermobility with a Beighton score of 6/9, alongside velvety hyperelastic skin and multiple abnormal atrophic/dystrophic scars.

Prior published cases show that kEDS-PLOD1 carries risk of fatal vascular events, including one patient who died from arterial rupture at age 14 and, across reports, aortic/arterial aneurysms in five patients of whom two died.
